changes.after: Skip a check when the Boolean answer is already known.

before: Rust conditions require Boolean expressions; a nonzero integer is not automatically a true condition.
&& skips its right operand when the left is false. || skips its right operand when the left is true.
The denominator check comes before division. A zero denominator makes the left side false and prevents evaluation of the division.
Short-circuiting determines which operations run, not just the final Boolean.
Expected output or behavior: true. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Trace which operands execute for zero and nonzero denominators. You may trace it without a Rust compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A Boolean value is true or false. Rust requires a Boolean condition. An integer alone does not count as true or false.
`&&` needs both checks to be true, so it skips the right check if the left is false. `||` needs either check to be true, so it skips the right check if the left is true.
The denominator is the number we divide by. `denominator != 0` checks it first. If the number is zero, the division on the right is skipped.
This early stop is called short-circuiting. The skipped operation does not run.
The screen shows `true`. The denominator is not zero, and 8 / 2 is greater than 2.
Set denominator to 0. The first check now decides the whole && expression.
